passages.note: Roll Call 58 is the Senate concurrence vote on SB 1(ss); Holdman is listed among the Yeas.

passages.provision_quote: before the earlier of viability of the fetus or twenty (20) weeks of postfertilization age of the fetus, if: (A) for reasons based upon the professional, medical judgment of the pregnant woman's physician, if either: (i) the abortion is necessary when reasonable medical judgment dictates that performing the abortion is necessary to prevent any serious health risk to the pregnant woman or to save the pregnant woman's life; or (ii) the fetus is diagnosed with a lethal fetal anomaly;
passages.note: Enrolled act text amending IC 16-34-2-1, the same instrument Holdman voted Yea on at concurrence.
Official bill-details/digest page; authored by Sen. Glick and sponsored by Rep. McNamara and Rep. King, not Holdman, so it is not his own act or words.

rows.reasoning: Holdman voted Yea on Roll Call 58 for SB 1(ss) (2022 Special Session), a single-subject 'Abortion' bill amending IC 16-34-2-1 so abortion is banned except where the abortion is necessary 'to prevent any serious health risk to the pregnant woman or to save the pregnant woman's life,' where the fetus has 'a lethal fetal anomaly,' or (within ten weeks) where the pregnancy results from rape or incest. This matches the rung to 'ban abortion except in cases of rape, incest, or a serious risk to the mother's life,' and excludes the rungs that keep abortion broadly legal or ban it with no exceptions.
